title: The digital age: Are we ready?
title_zh: 数字时代：我们准备好了吗？

section_a.title: Connection or Conversation?
paragraphs: On a quiet Saturday afternoon, Paul and his wife Maria are sitting at home reading their favorite books. Opposite to where they sit are their two sons: 15-year-old Jason and 12-year-old Jack, absorbed in playing chess. What’s the scenario here? The family calls it their “offline day”. From Friday night through Sunday evening, there are no video games, no computers, and no cell phones.

In our “always on” lives, such a scenario of family convention seems gone. Are we too immersed in the brilliance of the digital world? Perhaps. We cannot seem to resist the lure of our cell phones, even when we are in the company of others. Apparently, we have sacrificed conversation for connection.

At home, families sit together, texting, and reading emails. At work, executives text during board meetings. We also text when we’re on dates. Walking through a college library or the campus of a high-tech company, one sees an identical scenario: People are together, but each of them is in their own bubble, furiously connected to keyboards and tiny touch screens. The little devices most of us carry around are so powerful that they change not only what we do but also who we are.

It’s true we’ve already become accustomed to a new way of being “alone together”. Technology-enabled, we are able to be with one another, and also elsewhere, connected to wherever we want to be. We’ve been used to the idea of being in a tribe of one, loyal to our own party. In the silence of connection, we are comforted by being in touch with “invisible” friends and significant others, not too close, nor too far, just right.

A senior partner at a law firm describes vividly a scene in his office. Every morning, young associates would first lay out their suite of technologies: laptops, tablets, and multiple phones. Then they would put their earphones on. “Big ones. Like pilots. They have converted their desks into cockpits,” he said. With the young lawyers sitting in their cockpits, the office becomes quiet, a quiet that does not ask to be broken. They have completely plunged into their virtual world.

As we can see, there is no limit to time and space in this digital world. Connection can be anytime and anywhere. Gradually, we’ve picked up a habit of deletion – wiping out rich human relationships. The move from conversation to connection, for example, is part of this. In fact, online connection is often a deceptive illusion in which we cheat ourselves, assuming we’re not alone. Worse, over time we’ll stop caring and forget there is a difference between online connection and face-to-face conversation.

We are tempted to think that our little “sips” of online connection add up to a big swallow of real conversation. No, they don’t. Even though all of these sips have their places – in politics, commerce, romance, and friendship, I would claim, no matter how valuable they are, it’s impossible for them to substitute for real conversation, where people exchange ideas and share viewpoints dynamically.

Yes, connecting in sips may work for gathering discrete bits of information, or for saying “I am thinking about you”, or even for saying “I love you”, but it’s far from the adequacy of communication when it comes to understanding and knowing one another. Real conversation, on the other hand, is a more informative process, in which we’re more caring and observant. We hesitate and pause and go silent, and we reveal ourselves to one another through tones and nuances.

While communicating on our digital devices, we unconsciously raise our expectations as well. As we increase the volume and velocity of online connection, we start to expect acceleration – faster answers. We ask one another simpler questions; we dumb down our communication, even on the most important matters. Face-to-face conversation, by contrast, unfolds slowly, so it teaches us patience.

In addition, our move from conversation means diminished opportunities to learn skills of self-reflection. These days, social media continually asks us what’s “on our mind”, but we have little motivation to say something truly self-reflective. Imagine how hard it is to do something with thousands of online friends! It is through the conversation with trusted others that we learn to converse with ourselves – to be honest with ourselves.

I’m not a critic, but I am a partisan for conversation. To make room for it, I see some first steps. At home, we can create “sacred” spaces for conversation while doing domestic chores: the kitchen, the dining room. We can make our cars a place free of little devices. We can be a consultant to our children through the demonstration of the value of conversation. At work, we can do the same thing. Employees asked for casual Fridays; managers may “collaborate” and introduce conversational Thursdays.

Although an “offline day” may be unbearable for tech enthusiasts who need to alter their habits, experts say it is beneficial to assess both the merit and burden of digital technology. Let’s take some time away from the beeps and rings to evaluate our relationship with technology. Try to make some changes. At the beginning, it might be hard, but after a few months when a habit forms, we’ll begin to realize we have already gained a lot from it. So, look up, look at one another, and let’s start a conversation.

section_b.title: Living in the digital world
paragraphs: The technological advances that arrived in a swift fashion in the mid-1990s have reshaped the very fabric of society, and modern technologies have attracted various population groups in different areas. It is no exaggeration to say that technology has impacted upon the lives of everybody, in one way or another. However, this is often quite subliminal and somewhat ironic given the bold nature of the imposition of digital technology on our lives. It’s true that the digital world has changed our lives in almost every way possible.

To start with, do you still remember the days when teachers used chalk, dusters, and blackboards? They are almost never used today. Black has turned white, in the form of interactive whiteboards. To go one step further, the days of children having to carry a bag with printed books will probably be a distant memory in the future. With the advent of the age of the tablet, they are starting to use the impressive electronic devices to read e-books. More importantly, schools now come equipped with Wi-Fi or broadband to ensure instant Internet access for study and research purposes.

Likewise, how often do you see children playing games on a smartphone, laptop, or mobile game device of one kind or another? Probably more often than you see them playing outside with their friends. Children of the modern age are incredibly tech savvy, my goodness, almost from the time they learn to talk. They don’t have to learn how to use technology but are able to be informed, keeping abreast of the latest technological developments, because technology is simply a part of who they are. They grow up with it, they know it, and they cannot survive without it.

Dramatic changes can also be felt at home. As the modern family is busier than in the past, hectic family life seems dominated by all-things-convenient. Luckily, cooking is now made easy and a lot quicker thanks to hundreds upon hundreds of cooking apps, online recipes, how-to-cook videos, etc. Quite literally, technology has made cooking accessible and enjoyable to all. Furthermore, the days of battling other siblings for rights of the sole TV in the living room have gone and become a thing of the past. Now, children have their own laptop on which to watch their choice of TV shows, movies, videos, etc.

Then how about our workplace? Nearly a decade ago, one had to sit in the office all day long. Not so now though! Many companies, whether headquarters or affiliates, actively encourage working from home, and this is becoming more and more common as employers realize that employees do not require round-the-clock monitoring in the completion of their daily tasks. In addition, technology has led to the widespread use of online video conferences; as a result, colleagues are no longer obliged to even meet in a face-to-face environment, removing yet another element of the business arena of old.

Aligned with this fashion of convenience is our leisure. In the past, holidays were invariably booked through travel agents or a dedicated provider, based upon their sales skills and packages together with brochures. Sometimes, the most unappealing destination could be made to look like a luxurious five-star resort. Now, people are a lot more discerning, thanks to the abundance of online booking sites and online reviews of every leisure facility the world over. We search the Web to find the cheapest flights and avoid extra charges. We also book accommodations based upon our requirements and check out exactly what we will do before we even arrive!

In the everyday practicality, digital technology has also established its credibility in changing our old-fashioned personal life. While we used to stand in line at the bank during our lunch break, now we perform most of our banking online, mainly via our smartphones. While we formerly walked to the shop to buy the daily newspaper, now we can access news sites worldwide and download news apps at the touch of a screen. While we used to head to the video store to choose the latest release, now we can download movies online at the click of a mouse. While we used to play simple, yet wonderful, console games, now we can play them through the Internet against people from all around the world.

When it comes to social life, there are now so many social platforms cropping up that it’s difficult to keep up with them. It’s somewhat funny, though, that our social life is kind of akin to “emotional blackmail”. Even those who have desperately tried to evade all things social have found it’s simply impossible to avoid. Today people are more engaged in connection than conversation. Social media has become an essential part of life and a place for people to catch up with existing friends, rekindle friendships from the past, or meet new people from overseas …, because they can.

As we can see, the digital revolution has changed our lives to such an extent that the way we exist as a civilization has almost completely altered with no point in history for comparison. We concede that advanced technology is probably erasing rich human relationships, but it shows no signs of slowing down. It’ll continue to flourish and bring a lot of potential to transform the way we live in the foreseeable future. Are you ready for that?

section_c.title: A Smartphone Is All You Need
paragraphs: No cash? Your smartphone will do nicely. Chinese consumers who are used to spending their cash on technology are increasingly relying on a tech solution to pay for just about anything, from breakfast to booking a vacation.
To see how far I could go in Beijing without a wallet, I spent a day armed only with my smartphone.
A beautiful day started with a great breakfast. I paid for a local delicacy called jianbing at a food stall with my smartphone. By scanning a QR code, I transferred six yuan to the stall owner.
I then passed a small supermarket – each checkout counter carried a sign that proclaimed: “Welcome to use mobile payment!”

When it comes to transportation around the capital, you can order a cab or a private car through ride-hailing services. Mobile payment is accepted. If you don’t fancy waiting in traffic, there are also bikes for rent. You can unlock these bikes by scanning a QR code and pay a very cheap rent for the ride.

Many shops have incentives to use mobile payment services because this way they can engage customers better. After I paid for a sandwich and a cup of coffee at a restaurant with my smartphone, the waitress asked me to “follow” their public account so they could send me coupons and a virtual membership card. On the door of a nearby fashion boutique, there was another sign: “Welcome to use mobile payment!” Shops also accept credit cards, but not using mobile payment may be considered backward.
Mobile payment goes beyond daily purchases. You can also pay utility bills and credit card bills, or invest in money market funds.

From food stalls to shopping malls, almost every place I stopped by in this corner of Beijing accepted mobile payment. When making a purchase, all I needed to do is tap on the phone, scan the QR code, and make the payment in a second or two. Mobile payment has really changed the way of life in China. Chinese shoppers nowadays do not have to carry cash around; they just need to carry their phones around. Cash really is becoming a thing of the past.

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What activities are the family not allowed to do on their “offline days”?
questions.explanation: 原文第1段：从周五晚到周日晚上，全家不用电子游戏、电脑和手机；看书和下棋是他们正在做的事。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: According to Para. 3, to what extent are we influenced by the little devices most of us carry around?
options: They only affect how quickly we can answer messages.
They influence us mainly through the games we play.
They change not only what we do but also who we are.
They affect our health more than our relationships.
questions.explanation: 第3段结尾：这些小设备“so powerful that they change not only what we do but also who we are”，即既改变行为也改变人本身。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What does the author think of the idea that our little “sips” of online connection will substitute for real conversation?
options: The author agrees, because many small sips add up to a big swallow.
The author disagrees, saying sips can never substitute for real conversation.
The author thinks it depends on how valuable each sip is.
The author believes it is true only in politics and commerce.
questions.explanation: 第7段明确说“No, they don’t”，并强调再多的“小口”网络联系也不能 substitute for real conversation（取代真正的交谈）。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: According to Para. 8, what can we do in real conversation but cannot in online connection?
options: Gather discrete bits of information quickly.
Say “I am thinking about you” at any time.
Share viewpoints with thousands of online friends.
Understand and know one another through tones and nuances.
questions.explanation: 第8段：网络“小口”联系只能传递零散信息或问候，真正的交谈才让人通过语气和细微差别相互理解、认识。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What can a face-to-face conversation teach us?
options: It teaches us to expect faster answers.
It teaches us to gather more information.
It teaches us to type more efficiently.
questions.explanation: 第9段：面对面交谈“unfolds slowly, so it teaches us patience”，而网络联系让人期待加速、更快的回复。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What can we learn from the conversation with trusted others?
options: To converse with ourselves and be honest with ourselves.
To keep up with the latest technological developments.
To raise our expectations of online connection.
To avoid saying anything truly self-reflective.
questions.explanation: 第10段：正是通过与信任的人交谈，我们学会与自己对话、对自己诚实（learn to converse with ourselves – to be honest with ourselves）。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What is the author’s attitude toward conversation?
options: He is a critic who prefers online connection.
He is indifferent and sees conversation as outdated.
He is a partisan for conversation and urges us to make room for it.
He is confident that technology will replace conversation.
questions.explanation: 第11段开头：I’m not a critic, but I am a partisan for conversation. To make room for it, I see some first steps. 可见作者坚定支持交谈。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What is the author’s suggestion for evaluating our relationship with technology?
options: Ban all digital devices at home and at work.
Ask experts to monitor how much time we spend online.
Replace face-to-face conversation with online connection.
Take some time away from devices to assess the merit and burden of technology.
questions.explanation: 第12段：Let’s take some time away from the beeps and rings to evaluate our relationship with technology，并权衡数字技术的 merit and burden。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: He entered the film industry, taking small roles and writing ______ for a famous film company.
questions.explanation: scenario 除“可能发生的情况”外，还可指电影、戏剧的“剧情梗概”；为电影公司写“剧情梗概”用复数 scenarios。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: In doing translation, one should not ______ the meaning of the original to suit one’s own taste.
questions.explanation: alter the meaning 意为“改变原意”，与 to suit one’s own taste（迎合自己的口味）搭配。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: Without warning, there was a(n) ______ storm and the waves swept over the boat.
questions.explanation: furious 除“狂怒的”外，还可修饰 storm，表示“猛烈的、强烈的”。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: Doctors consider it their ______ duty to protect and save the lives of their patients.
questions.explanation: sacred duty 是固定搭配，意为“神圣的职责”；sacred 在此不表示宗教意义，而指“很重要的、深受尊重的”。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: The question was how to maintain that kind of ______ for a vehicle that weighed considerably more than 3,300 pounds.
questions.explanation: velocity 指“速度”，与 maintain（保持）搭配，说的是重量超过3,300磅的车辆如何保持那种速度。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: They are able to take ______ ideas, thoughts, and generalizations and weave them into meaningful patterns.
questions.explanation: discrete 意为“分开的、离散的”，discrete ideas 指零散的想法，与后文 weave them into meaningful patterns 呼应。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: They needed someone to ______ for a pianist who couldn’t make it, and her professor recommended her.
questions.explanation: substitute for sb. 意为“代替某人”；钢琴手来不了，需要有人替代。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: Let’s embrace Chinese culture this summer and get ______ in the richness of traditional Chinese music and dance!
questions.explanation: be / get immersed in sth. 意为“沉浸于、潜心于某事”，与 the richness of traditional Chinese music and dance 搭配。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: The Chinese scientific community will ______ with their international peers in frontier science research.
questions.explanation: collaborate with sb. 意为“与某人合作”，用于科研合作语境。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: At the end of the semester, students will be ______ on their proficiency in writing and speaking in English.
questions.explanation: assess sb. on sth. 意为“就某方面对某人进行评估”，此处用被动 be assessed on their proficiency。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: The ______ of the Internet and mobile devices means that anything that can be used effectively with them is likely to be a success.
questions.explanation: dominance 由 dominate + -ance 构成，意为“主导地位”；互联网和移动设备占主导，所以能借此有效使用的产品容易成功。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: Younger children may have problems paying attention in class, and would easily get ______.
questions.explanation: get distracted 意为“走神、分心”，distracted 是 distract 的过去分词作形容词，与 paying attention 形成对照。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: The competitive entrance examination for ______ to this university was such that hundreds of applicants were turned down each year.
questions.explanation: admittance 由 admit + -ance 构成，意为“准许进入”；admittance to this university 指入学许可。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: My dad is ______ and decides to devote his leisure time and energies to his passion: painting.
questions.explanation: retired 是 retire 的过去分词作形容词，意为“已退休的”；退休后才有闲暇投入绘画。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: Too much ______ on teachers telling them what to do next might hinder the development of children’s independent thinking.
questions.explanation: reliance 由 rely + -ance 构成，reliance on sb. 意为“对某人的依赖”，依赖老师会妨碍独立思考。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: Investors need ______ that the risk taken by the company is acceptable to them.
questions.explanation: assurance 由 assure + -ance 构成，意为“保证、担保”；投资者需要得到“风险可以接受”的保证。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: The careless ______ of trees could cause economic damage through degradation of the soil.
questions.explanation: clearance 由 clear + -ance 构成，意为“清除、砍伐”；滥砍树木会造成土壤退化带来的经济损失。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: Social media gives young people the avenue to make new friends and allows them to ______ contact with their old friends.
questions.explanation: maintain contact with sb. 意为“与某人保持联系”，与 make new friends 并列。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: We are quite familiar with the ______ of people sitting next to each other, not talking, but just staring at their phones.
questions.explanation: scenario 指“可能出现的场景”，此处指“相邻而坐却只盯着手机”的常见情景。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: Young people are more likely to be ______ in social media rather than spend time with their families and friends.
questions.explanation: be immersed in sth. 意为“沉浸于某事”，指年轻人沉浸在社交媒体中。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: With too many distractions, they cannot fully ______ on their tasks.
questions.explanation: concentrate on sth. 意为“专注于某事”，干扰太多就无法专心完成任务。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: Social media also leads to ______. Some people are crazy about likes and comments.
questions.explanation: obsession 意为“痴迷、着魔”，后文说有些人对点赞和评论痴迷到什么都愿意做。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: Everything they do, they want to post on social media to get some form of ______ from strangers.
questions.explanation: approval 意为“认可、赞许”，发帖是为了从陌生人那里获得某种认可。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: Since they cannot get the same popularity in real life as they do in social media, they yield to the ______ of social networks.
questions.explanation: yield to the lure of sth. 意为“屈服于某事物的诱惑”，lure 指社交网络的诱惑力。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: However, many of them live in ______ fear of being less popular.
questions.explanation: continual fear 意为“持续的恐惧”，continual 表示反复发生、持续不断。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: Everything falls apart when their popularity really ______, and they may even get into serious psychological problems.
questions.explanation: diminish 意为“减少、下降”；人气一旦真的下降，一切就崩塌，甚至出现严重心理问题。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: The creators of social networks perhaps did not ______ that their creations would bring these problems.
questions.explanation: anticipate 意为“预料、预期”，社交网络的创造者也许没有预料到会带来这些问题。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: The cheerful guy who wore virtual reality glasses ______ the virtual world.
questions.explanation: plunge into sth. 意为“投身于、沉浸于”，指戴上VR眼镜的小伙子完全进入虚拟世界。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: It has been the tradition in China that elderly people live in a familiar environment, preferably ______ their children.
questions.explanation: in the company of sb. 意为“在某人陪伴下”，指老人最好有子女陪伴。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: Chinese isn’t a subject that can be ______ in a month, and you can’t accomplish your goal of mastering the language unless you work at it for years.
questions.explanation: pick sth. up 意为“（无意间）学会（技能）”，指汉语不是一个月就能学会的科目。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: He ______ the map across the table and took another look at it.
questions.explanation: lay sth. out 意为“展开、铺开”，这里指把地图在桌上摊开再看一遍。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: The live music, the wild dancing, and the amazing lights all ______ an exciting theatrical experience.
questions.explanation: add up to sth. 意为“合计为、结果是”，三者合起来构成一场激动人心的戏剧体验。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: Since space is limited, we sometimes have to say goodbye to old things in order to ______ new items.
questions.explanation: make room for sb./sth. 意为“为…腾出空间”，空间有限时得清掉旧物给新物件腾地方。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: The magazine has a reputation for being very thorough, although critics claim that it has been ______ in recent years to cater to the mass market.
questions.explanation: dumb sth. down 意为“降低…的难度（使大众易懂）”，含贬义；评论家认为该杂志为迎合大众市场而降低了水准。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: This marks another historic step toward ______ the absolute poverty that has plagued the nation for centuries.
questions.explanation: wipe sth. out 意为“彻底消除”，wipe out absolute poverty 指消除绝对贫困。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What is ironic about digital technology as mentioned in Para. 1?
options: It develops very fast but people can keep up with it easily.
Some population groups get addicted to it while others are fed up with it.
It has invaded everything in our lives but we are not always aware of its impact.
Many people cannot live without it but deny that it has reshaped their lives.
questions.explanation: 第1段：数字技术对我们的影响往往是 subliminal（潜意识的），而它的强加于人又十分 bold，这种反差显得 ironic。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: Why may children not have to carry printed books in the future?
options: Children may use tablets to read e-books.
Children may become used to studying at home.
Children may be provided with interactive whiteboards in the classroom.
Children may leave their books in the classroom rather than bring them home.
questions.explanation: 第2段：With the advent of the age of the tablet, they are starting to use the impressive electronic devices to read e-books。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: Which of the following is not true about children in the digital world?
options: They are incredibly good at using electronic devices.
They can keep up with the latest technological developments.
They play games on electronic devices as often as they play outside with their friends.
questions.explanation: 第3段说孩子玩电子游戏的频率 probably more often than 在户外和朋友玩，因此“一样频繁”不符原文。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What changes does digital technology bring to the modern family?
options: The modern family is much busier.
People enjoy the convenience of ready-made food.
Cooking becomes easy and enjoyable to many people.
Siblings often battle for their choices of TV programs.
questions.explanation: 第4段：technology has made cooking accessible and enjoyable to all；A项是原因而非技术带来的变化，D项是过去的情况。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: Why do more companies encourage working from home?
options: It is an effective way to cut costs.
Employees can work more efficiently at home.
More companies are located far from the city center.
questions.explanation: 第5段：employers realize that employees do not require round-the-clock monitoring in the completion of their daily tasks。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What changes does digital technology bring to the leisure domain?
options: People prefer going to Internet-famous places.
People prefer watching shows online to traveling.
People become more discerning when booking their holidays.
People search the Web for what to do once they arrive at their destination.
questions.explanation: 第6段：Now, people are a lot more discerning, thanks to the abundance of online booking sites and online reviews。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What changes does technology bring to our social life?
options: People are more willing to make new friends.
People have learned to keep up with so many social platforms.
People find it simply impossible to avoid social interactions.
questions.explanation: 第8段：Even those who have desperately tried to evade all things social have found it’s simply impossible to avoid。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: According to the author, what will happen as a result of the digital revolution?
options: The pace of life will be much faster.
Our civilization will be changed little by little.
Our lives will continue to change in the future.
questions.explanation: 最后一段：技术虽在 erasing rich human relationships，但 It’ll continue to flourish and bring a lot of potential to transform the way we live in the foreseeable future。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: It seems that in-person connection has become less valuable than the digital one, which has es______ its cred______ in the eyes of young people.
questions.explanation: 原文搭配 establish its credibility：数字交流在年轻人眼中“确立了可信度”。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: Ironically, it is precisely our need for constant in-person interaction that plays an es______ p______ in fueling digital interaction.
questions.explanation: 原文搭配 play an essential part in：面对面交往的需求在推动数字交往中起“重要作用”。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: On the other hand, we are wired to love real and physical interaction, for the joy of sh______ v______ with someone face-to-face is not a deceptive illusion in any sense.
questions.explanation: 原文搭配 share viewpoints：面对面“交流观点”的快乐绝不是错觉。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: We are wired to love real and physical interaction, for the joy of sharing viewpoints with someone face-to-face is not a de______ il______ in any sense.
questions.explanation: 原文搭配 deceptive illusion：欺骗性的错觉，deceptive 意为“误导的、骗人的”。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: When faced with a choice between dropping by their office and shooting them an email, many of us may have lit______ mu______ for the former.
questions.explanation: 原文搭配 have little motivation for：对前一种做法“没什么动力”。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: As a consequence, we have di______ op______ for deeper communication.
questions.explanation: 原文搭配 diminished opportunities：进行深度交流的“机会减少”。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: Indeed, the wide______ u______ of digital technology in recent years has brought about dramatic changes to what we do and who we are.
questions.explanation: 原文搭配 the widespread use of digital technology：数字技术的“广泛使用”。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: The widespread use of digital technology in recent years has brought about dra______ ch______ to what we do and who we are.
questions.explanation: 原文搭配 bring about dramatic changes：带来“巨大变化”，与 to what we do and who we are 呼应。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: Digital technology has also com______ al______ our ways of interaction.
questions.explanation: 原文搭配 completely alter：彻底“改变”了我们的交往方式。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: If the march of digital interaction is inevitable in today’s hec______ l______, breaking the spell means knowing when digital or in-person interaction is the right way to communicate.
questions.explanation: 原文搭配 hectic life：在当今“忙碌的生活”中，数字交往的脚步不可避免。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: Breaking the spell means knowing how to re______ the l______ of digital communication when face-to-face conversation would be better.
questions.explanation: 原文搭配 resist the lure：在更适合面对面时“抵御数字交流的诱惑”。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: Face-to-face conversation is often the right way to communicate, although it often un______ sl______.
questions.explanation: 原文搭配 unfold slowly：面对面交谈“展开得慢”，正因如此才教会我们耐心。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: We believe this can help deal with the problem in the fore______ fu______.
questions.explanation: 原文搭配 in the foreseeable future：在“可预见的将来”。

questions.heading: Stories of China
questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How mobile payment has changed daily life in China
Why food stalls in Beijing attract foreign tourists
How to rent a shared bike in the capital city
Why credit cards are no longer accepted in shops
questions.explanation: 全文主旨：作者只带手机在北京生活一天，从煎饼摊到商场都能扫码支付，说明移动支付已改变中国人的生活方式（第1、8段）。

questions.heading: Stories of China
questions.question: What did the writer buy at the food stall for six yuan?
options: A sandwich and a cup of coffee
A box of fruit from a food stall
A coupon from a fashion boutique
questions.explanation: 第3段：作者在早点摊买当地小吃煎饼（jianbing），扫码转账六元给摊主。

questions.heading: Stories of China
questions.question: Why do many shops encourage customers to use mobile payment?
options: Because it saves them the cost of paper receipts
Because it helps them engage customers better
Because credit cards are no longer accepted
Because the government requires them to do so
questions.explanation: 第6段：商家有动力推广移动支付，因为这样能更好地维护顾客关系，例如请顾客关注公众号、发放优惠券和电子会员卡。

questions.heading: Stories of China
questions.question: How can people rent a shared bike in Beijing according to the passage?
options: By showing a passport at a rental office
By paying cash to the bike owner
By scanning a QR code with a phone
questions.explanation: 第5段：共享单车需用手机扫码解锁，租金很便宜；打车则是通过网约车服务，二者不要混淆。

translation.zh: 近年来，随着互联网技术的迅猛发展，互联网经济已成为一个热门话题。
translation.en_reference: In recent years, with the rapid development of Internet technology, the Internet economy has become a hot topic.

translation.zh: 以电子商务为代表的互联网经济已成为中国经济发展的重要引擎（driving force）。
translation.en_reference: The Internet economy, represented by e-commerce, has become an important driving force for China’s economic development.

translation.zh: 我国政府提出了“互联网+”的概念，以推动互联网与医疗、交通、教育、金融、公共服务等领域的结合。
translation.en_reference: The Chinese government has put forward the concept of “Internet Plus” to promote the integration of the Internet with health care, transportation, education, finance, public services and other fields.

translation.zh: 这将为互联网经济的发展提供更多发展机遇和更广阔的发展空间。
translation.en_reference: This will provide more opportunities and broader space for the development of the Internet economy.

writing.prompt: Write an essay of no less than 140 words on one of the following topics: Is smart technology making us dumb? / Will AI (artificial intelligence) cause mass unemployment? / Should parents monitor their children’s use of the Internet? The first topic has an outline that you can follow.
outline: Introduction: present the controversial argument that smart technology is damaging our cognitive abilities, then state the thesis that it is actually making us smarter.
Body: give three supporting points – smart technology helps us become more knowledgeable, helps us learn better, and helps us be more innovative.
Refutation: address the worry that smart technology is making us dumb and explain why it is not supported by scientific evidence.
Conclusion: restate the thesis that smart technology is changing our lives and benefiting us in positive ways.
